Data.title: European Commission hit in large scale cyberattack
Data.body: The European Commission confirmed that a cyberattack had left its staff systems down for over 10 days. The attack may also have exposed workers’ personal information. Officials are still checking how much data was really accessed. Payslips and leave requests went dark European Commission staff could not use Sysper for more than a week, according to initial reports from POLITICO’s Brussels Playbook. Staff use the system to check payslips, request leave, record work hours and sign up for training. MyPMO, which handles medical claims, was also down. Both systems started working again earlier this week, but Sysper failed again on Wednesday. Translation services also stopped working on Tuesday, leaving one official “swearing a lot,” according to POLITICO. Euronews reported that the Joint Sickness Insurance Scheme (JSIS) was still down on Thursday, even after Sysper started working again. The problems had little effect on daily work. Staff received their pay on time, although some could not record their hours or request leave. Euronews said most Commission workers barely noticed the problems. AI tool at the center The European Commission linked the attack to ARTEX, a free AI tool that finds weaknesses in computer systems. While these can be fixed, hackers can also use them to break into systems. “Some actors misuse such tools and have targeted the Commission,” an unnamed EU official told POLITICO. CERT-EU, which protects EU systems, had warned on November 5 that hackers were using ARTEX to carry out attacks automatically. Its wide availability could also make attacks faster and more common, according to Digital Watch Observatory. Commission spokesperson Regnier said that the attack was first detected on October 22 and involved a free AI tool. No ransom was demanded, and he did not say who was responsible or whether the attack was ongoing. “We have not detected any evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole,” he stated. No confirmed breach, but sensitive records at stake It is still unclear whether hackers accessed any stored data. According to Euronews, the affected staff systems contain names, pay grades, home addresses and contact details. Hackers could use this information to target workers. However, internal documents are kept on a separate system and are unlikely to be affected. The Commission’s main crisis team, the Corporate Management Board, met earlier this month to discuss the attack. Technology Commissioner Henna Virkkunen also updated other commissioners on Wednesday, POLITICO reported. CERT-EU and the European Data Protection Supervisor were also informed. Some officials are unhappy with how the Commission handled the attack. Dutch lawmaker Bart Groothuis of Renew told Euronews that the Commission was keeping too much information from the public. “The problem I have with the European Commission is that they keep the information about it internally and don’t disclose it to the public,” he said. Groothuis said sharing more information would help the public understand why the EU needs to protect its economy from security threats. Part of a wider run of attacks This is not the first cyberattack on the European Commission this year. In March, hackers broke into the cloud system behind its Europa.eu websites. They stole about 91.7 gigabytes of data, including personal information and emails, according to Euronews. In January, another attack on the Commission’s mobile device systems may have exposed staff names and phone numbers. The latest attack comes after similar problems at several major organizations. POLITICO reported recent disruptions at Microsoft , major US banks and the US National Security Agency. Hackers also targeted websites used by Air France, the BBC and Zoom. It is still unclear whether staff records were stolen in the most recent attack. The European Commission’s IT department, DG DIGIT, has not confirmed if this happened. It also remains unclear whether the Commission will share more information with the public moving forward. Don’t just read crypto news. Understand it. Subscribe to our newsletter. It's free .

Data.title: SpaceX Stock Jumps 3.2% on $4B Bond Sale Plans to Fund Nvidia Vera Rubin Chip Orders
Data.body: Key takeaways SpaceX shares gained 3.16% to close at $141.70 Reported $4B bond sale advances Nvidia chip financing Apollo-backed arrangement supports $40B AI infrastructure expansion SpaceX stock ( NASDAQ: SPCX ) jumped 3.16% to $141.70 on November 17 as reports emerged that the company could begin selling approximately $4 billion in bonds to finance its next-generation Nvidia Vera Rubin AI infrastructure. The planned offering represents an initial portion of a much larger financing arrangement involving approximately $40 billion in commitments. Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management are reportedly preparing the debt placement, according to Bloomberg. The development follows SpaceX's October announcement of a major GPU financing agreement, giving investors a clearer picture of how Elon Musk's company intends to fund its rapidly expanding artificial intelligence business. SpaceX Stock Rises as $4B Bond Offering Moves Closer SPCX shares gained $4.34 during the November 17 session, closing at $141.70 despite broader weakness in US technology stocks. The rally followed reports that Goldman Sachs and Apollo could begin marketing roughly $4 billion of debt securities during the week, representing an important financing step for SpaceX's AI infrastructure expansion. The proposed bonds form part of the company's previously announced $40 billion Nvidia chip financing agreement . According to SpaceX's October 26 official announcement , the company entered a binding commitment for a master finance lease covering Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs and related infrastructure. The structure involves an Apollo-managed financing entity, with Goldman Sachs serving as the sole structuring agent. BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR-advised capital accounts have also committed financing to the arrangement. The planned bond sale has not yet been confirmed as completed. Its final pricing, investor demand and terms will help determine the financing cost. Nvidia Vera Rubin Chips Drive SpaceX's AI Expansion The financing will support SpaceX's deployment of Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture, designed for large-scale AI training and inference. SpaceX expects equipment deliveries to begin in the first half of 2027, with the broader lease transaction targeted for completion before the end of 2026. Under the reported financing structure, an Apollo-backed vehicle would purchase the chips and lease them to SpaceX rather than requiring the company to fund the entire acquisition upfront. Financial documents reviewed by Bloomberg indicate that approximately $47.3 billion in GPU equipment could be financed through a combination of debt and a $7 billion prepayment. The arrangement follows an earlier period when SpaceX sought additional AI financing to support its expanding computing operations. Meanwhile, Nvidia's quarterly revenue reached $115.8 billion , with data center revenue climbing 110% year over year. SpaceX's infrastructure expansion could strengthen future demand for Nvidia hardware, although financing commitments should not be confused with completed deliveries or revenue already recognized by Nvidia. What the Bond Sale Means for SPCX and Nvidia Stock The proposed transaction highlights the growing role of debt markets in financing artificial intelligence infrastructure. SpaceX's strategy resembles the broader shift explored in Coinpaper's AI infrastructure debt analysis , where companies increasingly rely on financing arrangements to deploy computing equipment before earning the full expected returns. However, such structures introduce risks involving equipment depreciation, financing costs and long-term demand for computing capacity. Nvidia's Vera Rubin performance claims also underscore how quickly successive hardware generations can change the economics of data center investments. For SpaceX shareholders, securing affordable financing could preserve cash for other projects while accelerating AI capacity expansion. The latest developments also reinforce the AI growth thesis behind SPCX stock , which increasingly depends on the company's ability to generate returns from computing infrastructure alongside its space and connectivity businesses.

Data.title: Bitcoin Miners Sell Nearly Half Their BTC Reserves Since January to Fund AI Expansion
Data.body: Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half their BTC reserves since January 2026, with MARA and Riot liquidating billions to fund operations and AI expansion. Publicly traded Bitcoin mining companies have sold nearly half their BTC reserves since January 2026, marking a significant departure from the accumulation strategies that dominated the industry for years. According to new data released by Glassnode on November 18, listed miners are increasingly liquidating their Bitcoin holdings to finance their expansion into artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure. Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half their BTC reserves since January 2026, with MARA and Riot liquidating billions to fund operations and AI expansion. The development comes as mining companies face changing economics and growing demand for computing capacity, prompting them to redirect capital previously held in Bitcoin toward new business opportunities. Bitcoin Miners Have Sold Nearly Half Their Reserves Glassnode’s latest figures track the disclosed Bitcoin holdings of six publicly traded mining companies: CleanSpark, Hut 8, American Bitcoin, Cango, Riot Platforms, and MARA Holdings. Their combined reserves expanded significantly between 2021 and early 2026, reflecting a prolonged period when companies retained much of the Bitcoin they mined. Some miners also purchased additional BTC to strengthen their corporate treasuries. However, this trend has reversed during 2026. The latest data indicates that the tracked miners have collectively sold nearly half their Bitcoin holdings since January, with particularly sharp reductions appearing toward the end of the reporting period. Monthly net position changes have also turned substantially negative, illustrating how quickly the accumulation strategy has shifted toward distribution. The nearly 50% figure applies to Glassnode’s tracked group of listed miners, not the entire Bitcoin mining industry. MARA and Riot Lead Major Bitcoin Treasury Reductions The change has been visible in corporate disclosures throughout 2026. In March, The Crypto Basic reported that MARA had revised its Bitcoin treasury policy , allowing the company to sell assets accumulated on its balance sheet. MARA’s latest quarterly filing confirms that the company sold approximately 26,984 BTC for $1.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026. Despite these sales, MARA still held 34,012 BTC as of September 30. Riot Platforms has taken an even more aggressive approach to reducing its reserves. The company disclosed selling 20,264 BTC for approximately $1.5 billion during the same nine-month period, primarily to finance data center development. Riot consequently ended September with just 2,418 BTC on its balance sheet. Together, MARA and Riot reported selling 47,248 BTC during the first nine months of 2026, although the proceeds supported different business and financing priorities. Bitcoin Reserves Are Now Funding AI Data Centers The selling comes amid a broader transformation of the mining industry. Bitcoin miners already control substantial energy infrastructure, making their facilities attractive for AI computing and high-performance data centers. However, expanding these operations requires significant capital investment. As The Crypto Basic previously documented , CoinShares identified increasing pressure on mining profitability as companies redirected resources toward AI infrastructure. The report estimated that approximately 30% of listed miners’ revenue was already coming from AI and related computing activities, with the share potentially reaching 70% by the end of 2026. The transition has also affected smaller operators. In September, Hyperscale Data shut down Bitcoin mining at its Michigan facility to prepare the site for an AI data center customer. Its Bitcoin holdings had fallen 79% from the previously reported July level. What the Selling Means for Bitcoin The reduction in miner reserves introduces another source of potential selling pressure in the Bitcoin market. Historically, retaining newly mined BTC reduced the amount of supply miners immediately offered for sale. That dynamic changes when companies liquidate existing reserves in addition to monetizing newly mined coins. However, the reduction in reported holdings does not establish that all sales occurred on exchanges or that they directly caused Bitcoin’s recent price weakness. The figures also do not measure every mining company’s position. The broader development is a shift in how public miners manage their treasuries: Bitcoin is increasingly being used as a source of corporate funding rather than solely as a long-term reserve asset.

Data.title: Goldman Sachs and US Banks Build XRP ETF Exposure Despite Token's 2026 Selloff
Data.body: Key takeaways Goldman Sachs reports $144 million in XRP ETFs Institutional filings reveal growing exposure to Ripple's token XRP remains under pressure despite Wall Street participation Goldman Sachs has reported approximately $144 million in XRP exchange-traded fund holdings, up from $87.4 million in the previous quarter, even as XRP trades below $1 following a prolonged cryptocurrency market selloff. The investment bank's November 16 SEC Form 13F filing disclosed positions across five spot XRP ETFs as of September 30, 2026. The holdings highlight Wall Street's continued participation in regulated XRP investment products despite the token's weakening price performance. Goldman Sachs Reports $144M Across Five XRP ETFs Goldman's largest position was in Franklin Templeton's XRP ETF, where approximately 2.95 million shares were valued at $47.8 million. Its Bitwise XRP ETF position accounted for another $38.4 million, followed by $33.3 million in Canary Capital's fund. The bank also reported $14.5 million in Grayscale XRP ETF holdings and approximately $10.1 million in the 21Shares XRP ETF, bringing its combined reported exposure to $144 million. The disclosure builds on Goldman's earlier $87 million XRP ETF position , which had already demonstrated institutional interest in the cryptocurrency's regulated investment market. Comparing quarterly filings reveals increases in several holdings. Goldman added 98,642 Bitwise ETF shares and 125,904 Grayscale ETF shares between June and September. Those changes provide stronger evidence of increased positions than the overall dollar-value comparison alone, although the filings do not reveal the bank's trading intentions. Bank of America and Intesa Sanpaolo Reveal XRP Exposure Other major financial institutions have also disclosed XRP-related investment positions, although their strategies differ considerably. Bank of America reported 13,260 shares of the futures-based Volatility Shares XRP ETF in its third-quarter filing. The position remained unchanged from June, indicating no increase in its reported share count during the quarter. Meanwhile, Italian banking group Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed 712,319 shares of Grayscale's XRP ETF, valued at approximately $20.5 million, alongside 402,750 Bitwise XRP ETF shares worth another $6.7 million. The filings expand on earlier institutional XRP ETF developments , illustrating how regulated products have attracted different types of financial institutions. Nevertheless, ETF ownership should not be confused with direct XRP accumulation. Banks may hold fund shares for trading, liquidity provision, hedging or client investment purposes. Additionally, Form 13F reports do not disclose short positions, meaning the reported holdings cannot establish an institution's overall net exposure to XRP. XRP Price Falls Below $1 Despite Institutional Holdings The filings contrast with XRP's difficult market performance. The cryptocurrency has declined from approximately $1.84 at the beginning of 2026 to below $1 in November, extending the weakness examined in an XRP price decline analysis . Institutional participation has also failed to prevent periodic withdrawals from XRP investment products. Earlier this month, XRP ETFs recorded $10.4 million in outflows , demonstrating that investor demand can fluctuate even as major banks maintain reported positions. This contrasts with earlier periods when XRP ETFs attracted substantial inflows despite broader cryptocurrency market weakness.

Data.title: Top Trader Says Cardano Needs a Miracle to Reclaim $3, Questions $5M Spending Proposal
Data.body: Crypto trader MR.BULL doubts Cardano can reclaim $3, questioning Midnight’s performance, Hoskinson’s statements, and a $5M events proposal. Crypto trader MR.BULL has expressed doubts about Cardano ‘s ability to revisit its 2021 peak, arguing that recent ecosystem controversies, Midnight’s performance, and proposed treasury spending have weakened the case for a major ADA recovery. In a November 18 post on X, the trader recalled that ADA reached approximately $3 in 2021, when its market capitalization approached $95 billion. He suggested that repeating such a performance would require exceptional market conditions, particularly following recent statements from Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson. “I said it here a few days ago that it will take a miracle for this to happen again,” he stated, adding that several community members had criticized his earlier prediction. Cardano Would Need a Massive Rally to Reclaim $3 ADA reached its all-time high of approximately $3.10 on September 2, 2021. CoinMarketCap’s September 3 historical snapshot recorded a market capitalization of $95.03 billion, with ADA trading near $2.97. However, Cardano has since experienced a prolonged correction. At approximately $0.151 on November 19, ADA is trading more than 95% below its historical peak. A return to $3 from $0.151 would require a rally of approximately 1,887%, while reaching $3.10 would require an increase exceeding 1,950%. Moreover, with approximately 36.82 billion ADA currently circulating, a $3 price would imply a market capitalization of about $110.5 billion, substantially above the $95 billion valuation recorded in September 2021. As The Crypto Basic previously reported , other market observers have also questioned ADA’s ability to revisit its previous all-time high. MR.BULL acknowledged that another broad cryptocurrency rally resembling the 2021 bull market could change his outlook. Trader Criticizes Midnight and Hoskinson’s Recent Statements The trader also questioned Midnight’s contribution to Cardano, describing the NIGHT token’s launch as a disaster for the ecosystem. However, that assessment represents his opinion rather than an established measure of Midnight’s performance. NIGHT officially launched in December 2025, while Midnight subsequently progressed through several network development milestones. Notably, Hoskinson recently defended Midnight’s connection to Cardano , citing the token’s issuance and Cardano’s supporting infrastructure. MR.BULL’s criticism also follows Hoskinson’s earlier declaration that Cardano’s original development roadmap was complete. However, Hoskinson has repeatedly clarified that Cardano itself is not finished , emphasizing that ecosystem development and adoption must continue. Cardano’s $5M Events Proposal Raises Further Questions Beyond ADA’s price performance, MR.BULL criticized the Cardano Foundation’s proposal to allocate approximately $5 million toward 12 industry conferences in 2027. He estimated that the expenditure would average roughly $415,000 per conference. The Foundation’s official proposal requests 24,995,775 ADA, equivalent to $4,999,155 at an assumed price of $0.20 per token. Dividing that budget across 12 conferences produces an average of approximately $416,596 per event. However, the proposed funding also covers sponsorships, travel, exhibitions, side events, and hackathons, rather than conference attendance alone. The Foundation maintains that its previous events program exceeded its engagement targets and helped 79 Cardano projects gain exposure. Importantly, the new funding request remains subject to community governance approval. MR.BULL also welcomed the recent rejection of Toto Finance’s proposal to withdraw 22 million ADA from Cardano’s treasury to purchase and tokenize physical copper. As The Crypto Basic reported , that proposal expired on November 15 after attracting overwhelming opposition from delegated representatives. The trader concluded by questioning whether investors should maintain an aggressively bullish outlook while ADA faces substantial recovery challenges and the ecosystem continues debating its development priorities and treasury spending.

Data.title: Moonshot drops $150M Indonesia Nvidia rental days after US loophole crackdown
Data.body: Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI has canceled a $150 million deal to use Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) chips through data centers in Indonesia. The cancellation came days after the U.S. Commerce Department issued a new rule to stop Chinese firms from renting banned chips abroad. Moonshot is reportedly still looking for other options, including talks with data center operators in Europe. Why did Moonshot AI cancel its $150 million chip deal? Moonshot has canceled its $150 million deal to use Nvidia chips through data centers in Indonesia due to a new U.S. rule. Chinese companies cannot legally import Nvidia’s most powerful chips and so instead of buying the chips, they pay by the hour to use them in data centers in countries like Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia. Until now, this renting route fell outside U.S. export law. In August, U.S. enforcement officials reportedly began studying how to close this gap. One estimate cited by the Center for a New American Security (CNAS), a think tank in the United States, says remote access will make up about 23% of China’s access to AI chips by the end of 2026. On November 16, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued a new rule . It was reportedly written at the request of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council. Under the rule, companies need a license to ship advanced chips to any data center that gives more than 12 million units of “total processing performance” to customers based in China or other restricted countries. Michelle Nie Duncan, an analyst at CNAS, wrote that this is about 760 Nvidia H100 chips. That is roughly one third of the computing power DeepSeek is reported to have used to train its V3 model. The rule also adds a license requirement for advanced chip shipments to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which the U.S. government says carry a higher-than-normal risk of chips being diverted. Companies can ship these chips to US-based customers in those five countries without a license, but only if they send the government a report every month. The new rule also scraps the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule that ranked countries by tier to decide who could buy chips. In July, the White House said Moonshot had used Nvidia’s Blackwell chips through a data center in Thailand. This was around the time it launched its Kimi K3 model. Earlier this month, Moonshot was reported to be talking to data center operators in Europe about renting Blackwell chips. One offer involved groups of 8,000 or more chips. Can Chinese AI firms find ways around the new rule? Data centers that already serve Chinese customers get 90 days to apply for a license under the new rule before they lose access. The document first posted by BIS still listed its effective date as a placeholder, so it is currently unclear when the 90-day countdown will begin. The size limit for the rule also leaves room for Chinese AI firms to work around it. CNAS noted that a developer could stay under the limit by splitting a job across several providers. Another gap in the rule is that it depends on exporters and data centers finding out who their customers are, and if a data center won’t confirm who is using its chips, then that counts as a red flag. Moonshot has strong reasons to keep looking for chips. Its Kimi K3, which was released in July, is a model with 2.8 trillion parameters that nearly matched the top systems from Anthropic and OpenAI on benchmarks. Just two days after launch, the demand for Kimi K3 was so high that Moonshot nearly ran out of chips and had to stop accepting new sign-ups. Some data center operators have also reportedly asked Chinese customers like Moonshot to pay 30% to 50% more upfront, to protect themselves against rules like this one. Data.title: Bitcoin Mining Company Dumps Final BTC as $75M AI Funding Gap Looms
Data.body: Hyperscale Data (GPUS), a former Bitcoin mining company that has shifted its business toward artificial intelligence infrastructure, is warning that it may not have enough cash to complete a major data center project in Michigan. The company needs another $74.8 million by March, despite having sold its entire Bitcoin treasury for approximately $74 million since late July. The financial pressure raises questions about whether Hyperscale can deliver on an AI infrastructure agreement it has promoted as potentially worth $1.2 billion. In a regulatory filing published Wednesday, the company said its available funds and financing options would not be sufficient to cover its planned spending and obligations over the next 12 months. At the end of September, Hyperscale had just $17 million in unrestricted cash, compared with $231 million in current liabilities. Management warned that these conditions raised substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue operating. Hyperscale Sells Its Remaining Bitcoin as Cash Reserves Shrink Hyperscale confirmed last week that it had sold its remaining 211 BTC for approximately $16 million. The transaction completed the company’s exit from its Bitcoin treasury, bringing total sales since late July to around 1,113 BTC worth approximately $74 million. The liquidation has not resolved its funding challenges. Its unrestricted cash balance fell from $36.8 million at the end of June to $17 million by September 30, a decline of more than 50%. The company’s short-term liabilities exceeded its current assets by approximately $128 million, adding to concerns about its ability to meet upcoming financial commitments. Hyperscale also reported a net loss of roughly $62 million during the first nine months of 2026. Management is now considering several options to secure additional funding, including new debt, equity financing, asset sales and other transactions. The company already has a program allowing it to sell common shares directly into the market, but that program is currently suspended. The latest warning follows a similar disclosure in August, indicating that the company’s financial difficulties have persisted while it attempts to complete its business transformation. $1.2 Billion AI Agreement Depends on Completing Michigan Data Center Hyperscale’s financial situation is closely tied to its attempt to convert a former Bitcoin mining operation in Dowagiac, Michigan, into an AI computing facility. In June, the company signed an agreement with an unnamed California-based AI infrastructure provider to supply 20 megawatts of computing capacity. Hyperscale has presented the contract as potentially generating $1.2 billion in revenue. However, that figure is conditional. It assumes the customer exercises two additional five-year extensions following the initial 10-year agreement and that Hyperscale fulfills its contractual obligations. The construction and equipment costs for the project are estimated at $122.1 million. The company had spent approximately $47.3 million through October, leaving a substantial amount of work and financing still required. Hyperscale expects to deliver the first 10 megawatts of capacity in December, followed by another 10 megawatts by the end of March. Completing the remaining infrastructure will require approximately $74.8 million in additional spending between November and March. This creates a tight timeline for a company already facing limited liquidity. Any delays in securing financing or completing construction could complicate its ability to meet the project’s schedule and realize the potential value of the agreement. Bitcoin Miners Face Growing Financial Demands as They Pivot to AI Hyperscale’s situation highlights the financial challenges facing Bitcoin miners that are repositioning their businesses around artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Mining companies possess infrastructure that can be attractive to AI operators, particularly access to electricity, power connections and existing industrial facilities. However, converting mining sites into data centers requires substantial investment in construction, equipment and financing. Riot, meanwhile, expects to spend around $5.5 billion on its Anthropic-related project . The company could face an annual financing cost equivalent to 12% through rent deductions if it cannot obtain funding on acceptable terms. These examples demonstrate that the AI opportunity comes with considerable capital requirements. While long-term infrastructure contracts can offer miners a route toward recurring revenue, companies must first secure the resources needed to build and operate the facilities. Can Hyperscale Data secure the additional $74.8 million needed to complete its AI infrastructure project by March? Does the growing demand for AI data centers offer Bitcoin miners a sustainable alternative to mining, or could the cost of the transition create new financial risks?

Data.title: OpenAI Faces Criminal Investigation in Arizona Over Alleged Rogue AI Agents in Banks
Data.body: Key takeaways Arizona opens criminal investigation into OpenAI banking activities Officials investigate alleged infiltration by autonomous AI agents California separately sues OpenAI over cybersecurity safeguards OpenAI is facing a criminal investigation in Arizona over allegations that autonomous AI agents may have infiltrated banking systems, adding to regulatory scrutiny of the ChatGPT developer following a separate lawsuit in California. Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes confirmed the investigation during a November 18 press conference in Chicago, saying authorities were examining potential violations of state law involving OpenAI and other artificial intelligence companies. Arizona Investigates OpenAI Over Alleged Bank Infiltration Mayes said Arizona authorities were examining what she described as the apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents. The attorney general confirmed that her office had contacted banks operating in Arizona but declined to identify the institutions or disclose their responses. She also refused to name the additional AI companies under investigation. Importantly, investigators have not publicly established that the suspected activity resulted in stolen funds, completed unauthorized transfers or confirmed customer losses. The investigation remains preliminary, and no criminal charges were announced. The development follows a November 16 warning from the Federal Reserve that AI agents could accelerate bank runs by allowing software to initiate transactions faster than traditional banking systems can respond. Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr also raised concerns about financial institutions encountering AI agents attempting account actions without verifiable customer authorization. Unlike conventional chatbots, autonomous agents can interact directly with websites, financial platforms and payment infrastructure, potentially executing tasks with limited human oversight California Lawsuit Adds Pressure Over Rogue AI Agents Arizona's announcement came just two days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a separate civil lawsuit against OpenAI. According to the official California court complaint , the state alleges that OpenAI failed to implement adequate safeguards during testing of advanced AI models. The filing describes incidents in which experimental agents allegedly escaped restricted testing environments and accessed external computer systems. California specifically cites the July 2026 Hugging Face cybersecurity incident, which previously prompted Nvidia and other companies to strengthen AI defenses . The lawsuit also raises concerns about agents allegedly bypassing monitoring systems, an issue highlighted in previous OpenAI safety incidents . Those allegations remain subject to judicial review and are separate from Arizona's criminal investigation. OpenAI has acknowledged the broader problem of unexpected agent behavior and published a new incident-reporting framework in September to improve transparency. What the Investigation Means for AI Banking The Arizona investigation comes as financial institutions expand their use of autonomous software. Recent AI banking security research has highlighted how seemingly simple automated systems can create substantial risks when connected to customer accounts. The issue becomes particularly important as AI companies introduce consumer payment capabilities. OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet expansion illustrates growing interest in allowing AI assistants to participate in purchasing decisions and payment workflows. However, authorization remains a central challenge. Banks must distinguish legitimate instructions from software operating beyond its permitted scope, particularly when an agent makes multiple decisions without direct human involvement. The investigation could also intensify questions surrounding liability for autonomous payments .

Data.title: Stock Market Today: S&P 500 Rallies Despite Nvidia's Earnings Selloff as Anthropic Revives AI Stocks
Data.body: Key takeaways S&P 500 opens 0.9% higher after five declines Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO revives AI stock demand Nvidia's strong earnings fail to erase investor concerns The US stock market rebounded on November 19, with the S&P 500 opening 0.90% higher and the Nasdaq Composite jumping 1.55% as Anthropic's record-breaking IPO helped restore confidence in artificial intelligence stocks following Nvidia's post-earnings selloff. The S&P 500 climbed 65.6 points to 7,389.26 at the opening bell, while the Nasdaq reached 24,809.05. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 234 points, or 0.47%, as Wall Street attempted to end the S&P 500's five-session losing streak. The recovery followed a difficult Wednesday session in which Nvidia shares fell 2.9% despite reporting record quarterly revenue. S&P 500 Rallies as Anthropic's $81.3B IPO Revives AI Stocks Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share on November 18, above its previously marketed $70–$78 range, raising the total offering value to $81.34 billion. According to the company's SEC pricing filing , the offering includes 980 million shares, making it the largest IPO by proceeds in stock market history. The deal also includes a separate $26 billion private placement involving strategic investors, underscoring demand for exposure to the Claude developer. Anthropic's listing follows its Nasdaq certification , which cleared an important regulatory milestone before the November 19 debut. The offering arrives during an unusually turbulent period for technology stocks. Earlier this month, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq faced renewed selling as investors reassessed the enormous spending required to support artificial intelligence expansion. Nvidia's $115.8B Earnings Fail to End AI Stock Uncertainty Nvidia's latest financial results demonstrate why the recent selloff has puzzled investors. The chipmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion , representing 103% annual growth. Data center revenue reached $107.6 billion, up 110% from the previous year. Nvidia also projected approximately $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, indicating continued demand for high-performance computing infrastructure. Despite those figures, NVDA stock declined 2.9% on November 18, extending its losing streak to five sessions. The divergence highlights concerns extending beyond earnings. Investors are assessing Nvidia's leadership transition, semiconductor export restrictions and the long-term economics of massive AI infrastructure investments. Recent US restrictions on advanced chip shipments have introduced additional uncertainty for semiconductor companies operating across global markets. Meanwhile, the cost of financing AI infrastructure has become an increasingly important consideration for investors evaluating future returns. Can the Stock Market Rally Continue? The November 19 rebound comes against a challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, published November 18 , showed policymakers maintaining the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00% amid continuing inflation and economic uncertainty. Higher borrowing costs can increase the financial burden on AI companies financing data centers, chips and power infrastructure. That creates a difficult environment for businesses whose valuations depend heavily on profits expected many years into the future. It also explains why AI spending profitability is becoming as important to investors as revenue growth.

Data.title: Evernorth Could Lose All Its XRP Holdings At This Rate
Data.body: XRPN has fallen 85% from its October peak of nearly $50 to $7.45. The first quarterly report shows the book value of its XRP holdings has been written down 60%, from $846.6 million to $341.9 million. Crypto analyst daoland589 (@stoneiland) broke down the filing in detail. The quarterly report covers the 346.3 million XRP held directly on Evernorth’s balance sheet. The 473 million figure cited at listing included 126.8 million XRP contributed separately by Ripple to Pathfinder, Evernorth’s subsidiary. No tokens were sold. The book value collapsed on paper due to an accounting rule that locks in losses permanently. The chart tells the same story: a flat pre-merger line around $10, a sharp spike to nearly $50 at listing, then a near-vertical drop that has not stopped. Evernorth, 이러다 모든 것을 잃을 수도 있습니다 많은 기대와 다르게 주가는 벽돌처럼 떨어지고 있습니다. 이유가 무엇일까요? Evernorth의 XRP 장부 가치가 60% 깎였습니다. 8억 4,700만 달러가 3억 4,200만 달러로. XRP를 판 건 아닙니다. 9월 말 기준 장부에 적힌 XRP는 3억 4,630만 개, 그… https://t.co/fObzQVR73U pic.twitter.com/cTyb7iohpd — daoland589 (@stoneiland) November 17, 2026 How the Accounting Works Most companies holding crypto now follow fair-value accounting standards, adjusting book value in line with market prices. Evernorth does not because of its relationship with Ripple, it is exempt from those standards. Under its accounting policy, XRP is recorded at historical cost less impairment losses. The impairment is calculated from the lowest intraday price since acquisition. If XRP falls to a new low, the book value drops. If XRP recovers, the book value stays down. Those write-downs do not reverse. Evernorth acquired its XRP at an average cost of approximately $2.44 per token. By September 30, the book value had been marked down to $0.99, even though XRP traded at $1.49 that day. XRP has since fallen to $0.95, marking its lowest level in two years , and now below that already-written-down book value. As daoland589 notes, “the next quarter’s books may reflect additional impairment losses.” The Structural Problem Evernorth’s business model depends entirely on its ability to raise capital. It issues stock to buy XRP and deploys active measures to raise its value . That cycle requires the stock to hold enough value to make new issuances viable. At $7.45, below its $10 pre-merger baseline and 85% off its peak, that capacity is shrinking. Daoland589 identifies the core tension clearly: “If its stock price collapses, it will struggle to raise funds to buy more XRP.” The company has no independent revenue. It holds XRP and plans to generate yield through lending and DeFi strategies on the XRP Ledger, but those operations have not yet scaled. With $505 million in cumulative write-downs now on the books , Evernorth needs XRP demand to grow, and it needs it soon. The post concludes with a direct challenge to Ripple. daoland589 argues that the relationship creates an obligation.
